newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast spot prods prices firm amid supply dip.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast spot prods prices firm amid supply dip.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast refined petroleum products rose modestly in active trade Tuesday, lifted by news of a slight decline in the high volume of regional inventories, traders said.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) reported what some traders called a "disappointing" drop in West Coast gasoline stocks. Stocks fell 226,000 barrels to total 28.8 million barrels, API showed in its weekly stock report.

But the lower supplies were offset by high rates of production from West Coast refineries. Refinery use rose by 2.4 percentage points to 97.8 percent of total plant capacity, compared to about 85 percent use a year ago.
"Expectations were for a much more bullish refinery number. Production is still really high," a refinery trader said.

Meanwhile, New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) energy futures, saw August crude oil up 68 cents a barrel to $19.67 a barrel. Crude oil futures generally influence the West Coast spot markets, along with product futures.

July CARB gasoline sold to refineries in Los Angeles at 56.50 cents and 56.75 cents a gallon, traders said. August traded at the same level. The grade was talked between 56.50 and 57.50 cents, a half cent higher than Monday.
CARB diesel was talked between 56 and 57 cents a gallon, up one cent from yesterday. Jet fuel stood 55/56 cents, a half cent over Monday.
State-mandated CARB gasoline cost one cent more in San Francisco, where at least 10 large-sized cargoes of product have left the market since May, tightening supply, traders said.
